definitions.explanation: An area of land designated for burying the dead, typically containing gravestones and memorials.

examples.japanese: {墓地|ぼち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れた→訪れる：07678_otozureru⟧。

examples.english: My grandfather's grave is in the town cemetery.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{盆|ぼん}→お盆：05587_obon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{墓地|ぼち}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}って→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦{墓参|はかまい}り→墓参り：10663_hakamairi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{毎年|まいとし}→毎年：00731_maitoshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{習慣|しゅうかん}→習慣：01429_shuukan⟧だ。
examples.english: Every year during Obon, our family makes it a custom to visit the cemetery and pay respects at the grave.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {墓地|ぼち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れる→訪れる：07678_otozureru⟧: to visit a cemetery
- {市営|しえい}{墓地|ぼち}: municipal cemetery
- ⟦{共同|きょうどう}→共同：02591_kyoudou⟧{墓地|ぼち}: communal cemetery
- {墓地|ぼち}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{管理|かんり}→管理：00178_kanri⟧: cemetery maintenance

CULTURE: In Japan, most cemeteries are associated with Buddhist temples (⟦{寺院|じいん}→寺院：00122_jiin⟧{墓地|ぼち}). Municipal and private cemeteries also exist. Visiting family graves (⟦{墓参|はかまい}り→墓参り：10663_hakamairi⟧) is an important custom, especially during Obon and the spring/autumn equinoxes (⟦{彼岸|ひがん}→彼岸：12612_higan⟧).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {墓地|ぼち}: general term for cemetery or burial ground
- ⟦{霊園|れいえん}→霊園：19164_reien⟧: memorial park, garden cemetery (more modern, park-like)
- ⟦{墓場|はかば}→墓場：05876_hakaba⟧: graveyard (slightly more informal or literary)
